The exact rating/grade given for Tidal by Robert Christgau Robert Christgau gave Fiona Apple's "Tidal" album a "Neither" rating. This is not a letter grade but rather one of Christgau's special ratings indicating albums he does not recommend. ## Detailed Findings ### Source Information - **URL**: https://www.robertchristgau.com/get_artist.php?name=Fiona+Apple - **Date accessed**: Current session - **Page content**: Successfully retrieved and parsed ### Exact Rating for Tidal The "Tidal" album appears twice on the Fiona Apple page, both times with the same rating: 1. **Line 87** (in album list): ```html
  • Tidal [Work, 1996]
    • ``` 2. **Line 94** (in Consumer Guide Reviews section): ```html

    Tidal [Work, 1996]

    ``` ### Rating Type - **Rating**: "Neither" (displayed as an image with alt text "Neither") - **Format**: Not a letter grade, but a special Christgau rating - **Meaning**: Albums rated "Neither" are ones Christgau does not recommend ### Comparison with Other Albums For context, here are the ratings for Fiona Apple's other albums on the same page: - "When the Pawn..." (1999): A- - "Extraordinary Machine" (2005): A- - "The Idler Wheel..." (2012): A- - "Fetch the Bolt Cutters" (2020): A This confirms that "Neither" is distinctly different from Christgau's standard letter grade system. ### Methodology - Used Python with requests and BeautifulSoup to fetch and parse the webpage - Searched for the specific album "Tidal" and its associated rating - Verified the rating appears consistently in multiple locations on the page - Cross-checked with other album ratings to confirm the rating system The "Neither" rating is Christgau's way of indicating that while he may have listened to the album, he does not consider it worth recommending to readers.

function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 -c "
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

url = 'https://www.robertchristgau.com/get_artist.php?name=Fiona+Apple'
response = requests.get(url)
soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, 'html.parser')

# Look for album information, specifically for Tidal
print('=== Robert Christgau - Fiona Apple Page ===')
print(f'URL: {url}')
print(f'Status: {response.status_code}')
print()

# Find all album entries
album_sections = soup.find_all('div', class_='album') or soup.find_all('table', class_='album') or soup.find_all('div', id_='album')
print(f'Found {len(album_sections)} potential album sections')

# Look for text containing 'Tidal'
text_content = soup.get_text().lower()
tidal_matches = []
lines = text_content.split('\n')
for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    if 'tidal' in line.lower():
        tidal_matches.append((i, line.strip()))

print()
print('=== Lines containing \"Tidal\" ===')
for line_num, line in tidal_matches:
    print(f'Line {line_num}: {line}')

# Look for rating patterns (A+, A, A-, B+, B, B-, C+, C, C-, D+, D, D-, E, etc.)
rating_patterns = ['A\\+', 'A-', 'A', 'B\\+', 'B-', 'B', 'C\\+', 'C-', 'C', 'D\\+', 'D-', 'D', 'E', 'Neither', 'Honorable Mention']
print()
print('=== Looking for rating patterns near Tidal mentions ===')
for line_num, line in tidal_matches:
    for i in range(max(0, line_num-3), min(len(lines), line_num+4)):
        for pattern in rating_patterns:
            import re
            if re.search(pattern, lines[i]):
                print(f'Line {i}: {lines[i]}')
                print('---')
""}

When the Pawn . . . [Clean Slate/Epic, 1999]
96: For any Upper West Side showbiz kid, musical comedy is mother's milk, more "natural" than the rude attack of rock or the polite confessional of folk. And having gone mega, Fiona was autonomous enough to want it that way. With crucial help from Jon Brion, she's got the Richard Rodgers/Kurt Weill part down, and will surely tackle the Dorothy Fields/Lorenz Hart part later. Meanwhile, confessional attacks like "A Mistake" and "Get Gone" will do. Webber & Sondheim, watch out. A-

97:

Extraordinary Machine [Clean Slate/Epic, 2005]
98: Instead of delivering the music a sharp-tongued breakup record by an empowered young female would imply--if not folk-rock plain and simple, then emotional piano-woman pop--Apple adapts Broadway show tune to confessional mode. Although Mike Elizondo adds momentum, Jon Brion's colors still predominate, and the melodic and structural contours are all Apple's. Ira Gershwin she's not; Betty Comden she's not either. But she wouldn't be half as inspiring if they were what she was aiming for. A-

99:

The Idler Wheel Is Wiser Than the Driver of the Screw and Whipping Cords Will Serve You More Than Ropes Ever Do [Epic, 2012]
100: A funny thing will happen once you've figured out that the title is the stupidest thing about an album that's damn catchy after all. It'll sound like a piano record--a defiantly primitivist, raucously avant-garde lounge singer's piano record, with a really nutty drummer: he'll-bang-on-anything (and-get-her-to-pitch-in) producer Charley Drayton. There are few arpeggios, and not much tone color and such. She just executes simple figures and hammers thick chords, including a few boogie-woogies just to make a point. She also sings--words, yes, but more decisively, sounds. Not background music. But you could sure call it mood music. A-
